cards.title: Grid & Downforce
cards.body: Internal combustion before it was regulated into politeness. Aerodynamics as an argument between drag and grip. And tyres — the only four patches of rubber that decide whether any of the rest of it mattered.

cards.title: Ninety Minutes, Five Days
cards.line: Football and cricket, at opposite ends of patience.
cards.body: One sport compresses everything into a single afternoon. The other stretches it across five days and calls a draw an outcome. I follow both, and I'll defend both formats to anyone who asks.

cards.title: Everything in the Signal
cards.body: A verse that argues with itself and a string section that never says a word — I don't think those are different interests. Both are structure carrying weight. The playlist has no genre discipline whatsoever.

cards.title: Two Kinds of Play
cards.body: Slow games I play for the world — the ones where riding somewhere quietly is the point. Fast games I play for the read: tactical first-person shooters and battle royale, where the whole match turns on one correct guess.

cards.title: Borders Are Recent
cards.line: Empires, cultures, and how they drifted.
cards.body: A geography habit that turned into a history habit. How trade routes became languages, how empires left their grammar behind, how a line drawn in one century is still deciding things in another.

cards.title: The Older Engineering
cards.line: Animals, biology, and systems nobody designed.
cards.body: Every organism is an optimisation problem that has been running for millions of years without a specification. I find that more interesting than most architecture diagrams.

cards.title: The Part People Touch
cards.line: UI, UX, and interfaces that don't argue back.
cards.body: I care about the layer underneath — but the layer on top is where a system either earns trust or loses it. Good interfaces are invisible in the same way good infrastructure is.

cards.title: Issmam's Photography
cards.line: Standing still long enough to notice.
cards.body: Started with school magazines and workshops, kept going. An archive that goes back further than the gear deserved.
